anchorClaim: In low-income countries from 2010-2020, reductions of 20% or more in international vaccine funding correlate at r>=0.5 with declines in national vaccination coverage rates within 2 years.
confidenceSummary: Grade C reflects a moderate but insufficient evidence base. Only four studies address the claim, none designed to test causation directly, and most findings depend on context. The record remains open.

datoms.claim: The paper does not measure the correlation between international vaccine funding reductions and vaccination coverage rate declines in low-income countries during 2010-2020.
datoms.source: P. Berman. "Immunization financing in developing countries and the international vaccine market: trends and issues" (2004). doi:10.1590/S0042-96862004000900017

datoms.claim: Low- and middle-income countries with HPV vaccination programs achieved lower final-dose coverage rates than high-income countries due to higher dropout rates between first and final doses.
datoms.source: Laia Bruni, Anna Saura-Lázaro, Alexandra Montoliu, María Brotons, Laia Alemany. "HPV vaccination introduction worldwide and WHO and UNICEF estimates of national HPV immunization coverage 2010-2019" (2020). doi:10.1016/j.ypmed.2020.106399

datoms.claim: The paper does not measure the correlation between international vaccine funding reductions and vaccination coverage declines; it measures vaccine effectiveness against antibiotic-treated illness outcomes.

datoms.claim: In low-income and middle-income countries, measles vaccination coverage declined or stagnated in more than half of districts between 2010 and 2019, following gains from 2000 to 2010.
datoms.source: Local Burden of Disease Vaccine Coverage Collaborators, Alyssa N. Sbarra, Sam Rolfe, Jason Q. Nguyen, Lucas Earl. "Mapping routine measles vaccination in low- and middle-income countries" (2020). doi:10.1038/s41586-020-03043-4

guide.whatScienceSays:
DATOM found only 4 studies that speak to this claim, far short of what a question like this needs. None was designed to test whether cutting international vaccine funding actually causes coverage to fall. The honest answer today is that there is not enough evidence to judge it either way. That is what the "Insufficient record" verdict means, and the Grade C reflects how limited the evidence base remains.

The few related studies DATOM did find appear below, tagged by what they looked at.
guide.howConfident:
The Grade C reflects a moderate evidence base that remains too small to support a clear verdict. Only 4 studies address this claim, and none was built to isolate the causal effect of funding cuts on vaccination coverage.

The single decisive study pointed against the claim, but one study cannot settle a question this important. The remaining studies found conditional or context-dependent relationships, meaning the answer depends on factors the research has not yet pinned down. Until more direct evidence arrives, the record stays open.
decisionSupport: Only 4 studies in the entire corpus address whether cutting international vaccine funding causes coverage rates to drop.
None of the 4 studies was designed to test the causal claim directly.
One decisive study pointed against the claim, while zero pointed in support.
Three studies found conditional relationships, meaning the outcome depends on circumstances the research has not yet clarified.
The evidence base is too small and indirect to support a verdict in either direction.
guide.faultLines:
Study Design Mismatch: None of the 4 studies was built to isolate whether funding cuts cause coverage drops. Most examined correlations or looked at related factors without controlling for the many variables that affect vaccination rates in low-income countries.

Conditional Findings Dominate: Three of the 4 studies found that the relationship depends on context, implementation details, or other factors. Without knowing which conditions matter most, the evidence cannot support a clear answer.

Single Opposing Study: The one decisive study pointed against the claim, but a single study cannot override the broader uncertainty. More research designed to test causation directly is needed before the record can close.

name: Vaccination Coverage Equity and Health System Financing
plainQuestion: Cutting international vaccine funding causes vaccination coverage rates to drop in low-income countries.
scope: Studies looked at low and middle-income countries, mostly between 2010 and 2019 (one source is from 2004, outside that range). The people studied range from children under 5 to teenagers, and in some cases the age group isn't specified.
metric: How much countries spend on vaccine programs over time, how many children get measles and HPV vaccines, and how many illness cases are prevented by vaccination.
